SCORING METHOD (how every score on this tab is built)
10 = IOC 2018 / AIS Group A with meta-analysis support; 5-7 = AIS Group B or small positive RCTs; 2-4 = AIS Group C or mixed; 0-1 = no evidence or prohibited.

Sport certification 0-40 (Informed Sport/NSF/BSCG/HASTA across many products 40; a few lines 30; Informed Choice only 20; Cologne List 15; own lab screening 8; none found 0) + independent label tests 0-25 (passed 25, none known 12, failed 0) + regulatory/legal record 0-20 (clean in searches 20; advertising/pricing rulings 15; product class actions or recalls 10; serious safety case or failed test 0-5) + transparency 0-15 (full doses, no proprietary blends 15; mixed 8; blends 0).

Certifications are PRODUCT- and BATCH-specific: always check the exact product and batch on the certifier's site before use. 'Not found' means not found in this build's searches (checked 1 Nov 2026), not proof of absence. Brand scores are not a judgment of taste or price.

Effects of the main ergogenic aids (caffeine, creatine, nitrate, bicarbonate) are broadly similar by sex, but women are under-studied (e.g. only 11 of 149 bicarbonate studies analysed women). Female-specific priorities: energy availability, iron, calcium/vitamin D, protein timing by cycle phase and menopause, caffeine with the pill.
Discuss supplements with a sports physician or accredited sports dietitian, especially for under-18s, pregnancy, medicines or health conditions.

cols: How to use in this system
rows: Gradually increasing the demand on the body over time (load, reps, sets, range, density, or difficulty).
Everything — strength, size, endurance, tendon, bone. Without it adaptation plateaus.
The body adapts only to a stress it isn't already used to; once adapted, the same stimulus becomes maintenance.
Add load (~2–10%) once you hit the top of your rep range at the target effort, or add 1–2 reps / 1 set / harder variation.
Use Phase_Gates to decide when to progress; log reps × load each session and move up when all sets hit the top of the range.
Adding load every session regardless of form or recovery; changing exercises so often that progress can't be tracked.
ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training, Med Sci Sports Exerc 2009;41(3):687-708. Kraemer & Ratamess, Med Sci Sports Exerc 2004.
Specific Adaptation to Imposed Demands — you get better at exactly what you train (movement, speed, range, energy system).
The trained pattern, joint angle, velocity and metabolic pathway.
Neural coordination, fibre recruitment and metabolic enzymes adapt to the exact task.
Match ≥50–70% of training to the goal task; general work fills the rest.
Use Sports_Demands + Sport_Drills to make sure combos match the sport's speed, range and energy system.
Training only slow/general work and expecting fast/specific performance.
ACSM 2009 Position Stand. Behm & Sale, Sports Med 1993 (velocity specificity).
Training causes temporary fatigue; with recovery the body rebuilds slightly above baseline (supercompensation).
Muscle protein synthesis stays elevated ~24–48 h after a session; glycogen, nervous system and connective tissue recover on different timelines.
Same muscle hard again after ~48–72 h; light/technical work can be daily.
Day_Planner should space hard sessions for the same muscle group ≥48 h apart.
Judging a session by how sore or exhausted you feel — fatigue is not the goal, adaptation is.
Damas et al., J Physiol 2016;594(18):5209-22. MacDougall et al., Can J Appl Physiol 1995 (MPS time-course).
How many reps you leave 'in reserve' at the end of a set. RPE 10 = failure, RPE 8 ≈ 2 reps left.
Controls how strong the stimulus is and how much fatigue it costs.
The last reps before failure recruit the highest-threshold motor units → strongest growth signal.
Hypertrophy: 0–3 RIR. Strength: 1–4 RIR. Failure is optional — similar gains at 1–3 RIR with less fatigue.
Write target RIR next to each combo (e.g., 3×8 @ RIR 2). Use failure only on last set of safe/machine exercises.
Going to failure on heavy compound lifts every set; or stopping 6+ reps short and calling it 'hard'.
Refalo et al., Sports Med 2023;53:649-65. Grgic et al., J Sport Health Sci 2022;11(2):202-11. Zourdos et al., J Strength Cond Res 2016;30(1):267-75.
Training volume (sets per muscle per week)
Number of hard sets (≈ within 0–4 RIR) per muscle group each week.
Main dose driver for hypertrophy; secondary for strength.
More mechanical-tension exposure = more growth signal, with diminishing returns.
Minimum effective: ~4 sets/wk. Most growth: ~10–20 sets/wk. Beyond ~20 → diminishing returns and higher fatigue.
Session_Builder: total weekly hard sets per muscle and keep within 10–20 for priority muscles.
Counting warm-up sets; jumping straight to 25+ sets.
Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger, J Sports Sci 2017;35(11):1073-82.
How often a muscle or skill is trained per week.
Muscle protein synthesis returns to baseline ~36–48 h → spreading volume keeps quality high.
≥2×/week per muscle is a good default. When weekly volume is equal, frequency matters little.
If weekly sets per muscle exceed ~10, split them over 2–3 days.
Doing 20 sets for one muscle in a single session.
Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger, Sports Med 2016;46(11):1689-97. Schoenfeld et al., J Sports Sci 2019 (volume-equated frequency).
Planned variation of volume and intensity over weeks/months (linear, undulating, block).
Rotating emphasis lets one quality build while others are maintained, and manages accumulated fatigue.
Blocks of 3–6 weeks; daily/weekly undulating is equal or slightly better for strength than fixed loading.
Phase_System + Phase_Dose already implement this — keep each phase focused on 1–2 primary qualities.
Changing everything every week (no consistent stimulus).
Williams et al., Sports Med 2017;47(10):2083-100 (periodized vs non-periodized meta-analysis). Rhea & Alderman, Res Q Exerc Sport 2004.
A planned lighter week (≈40–60% less volume or intensity).
Fatigue disappears faster than fitness, so a short reduction reveals gains (fitness–fatigue model).
Every 4–8 weeks, or when performance drops 2 sessions in a row with high RPE.
Insert after each Phase_System block or when readiness flags appear.
Never deloading; or deloading so long (>2 weeks) that you lose fitness.
Bell et al., Sports Med Open 2022 (coaches' deloading practices). Mujika & Padilla, Sports Med 2000;30(2):79-87 & 30(3):145-54 (detraining).
How fast fitness is lost and the least training needed to keep it.
VO2max declines within 2–4 weeks; strength and muscle are retained longer.
Maintain strength/size: ~1 hard set per exercise, 1×/week at the same intensity. Maintain VO2max: keep intensity, cut frequency up to 2/3 and volume up to 1/3–2/3.
Use as 'minimum session' template in Day_Planner on busy days.
Stopping completely instead of doing a minimum dose.
Spiering et al., J Strength Cond Res 2021;35(5):1449-58. Mujika & Padilla, Sports Med 2000.
People respond differently to the same program.
Explains why a template isn't perfect for everyone.
Genetics, training history, sleep, nutrition, stress all modify the response.
Track your own data for 6–8 weeks before judging a method.
Use Testing_Protocols every 4–8 weeks to see what works for YOU.
Copying an elite program and blaming yourself when it doesn't fit.
Ahtiainen et al., Age 2016 (individual hypertrophy response). Bouchard et al., HERITAGE Family Study, J Appl Physiol 1999.
Contracting a muscle without the joint moving (e.g., wall sit, plank, mid-thigh pull, Copenhagen hold).
Strength at the held angle (± ~15–20°), tendon stiffness, joint stability, posture endurance, short-term pain relief in some tendon problems.
High force with little joint motion → large tendon load with low joint stress. Long-muscle-length holds transfer to a wider range than short-length holds.

Max strength: 3–5 s holds at 80–100% effort × 3–5 reps. Tendon: 4–5 × 30–45 s at ~70% effort. Endurance/posture: 20–60 s at moderate effort. Hypertrophy: longer holds near long muscle length, accumulating ~60–90 s per set.
Tag combos with joint angle. Prefer long-length holds (e.g., deep split squat hold) for broad transfer; use in warm-ups, rehab and Phase 1.
Holding only at the easiest angle; breath-holding (raises blood pressure — breathe steadily).

Oranchuk et al., Scand J Med Sci Sports 2019;29(4):484-503. Kubo et al., J Appl Physiol 2001;91(1):26-32. Rio et al., Br J Sports Med 2015;49(19):1277-83. Holden et al., Scand J Med Sci Sports 2020 (analgesia not superior to isotonic).
Controlling the lengthening phase — slow negatives, Nordic curls, heavy eccentrics.
Strength, muscle length (fascicle length), tendon resilience, hamstring injury prevention.
Muscles can produce ~20–50% more force eccentrically, with lower energy cost; strong stimulus for structural change.
Nordics: 2–3 × 4–8, 1–2×/week. Slow negatives: 3–5 s lowering. Expect soreness for first 1–2 sessions (repeated bout effect protects after).
Use Nordics/eccentric variants in Phase 1–2 and in-season for injury prevention.
Starting with high volume eccentrics → severe soreness; very slow (>8 s) reps reduce total work.
Roig et al., Br J Sports Med 2009;43(8):556-68. van Dyk et al., Br J Sports Med 2019;53(21):1362-70 (Nordics ≈51% fewer hamstring injuries). McHugh, Scand J Med Sci Sports 2003;13(2):88-97.
How fast each phase of the rep is done.
Power (fast concentric), control and time under tension.
Hypertrophy is similar across 0.5–8 s per rep; intentionally fast concentric gives better strength/power.
Lift (concentric) as fast as possible with control; lower in 1–3 s. Avoid >8 s reps for hypertrophy.
Default tempo: 'controlled down, fast up'. Use slow tempo only for technique or rehab.
Super-slow reps for size (no added benefit, lower load).
Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger, Sports Med 2015;45(4):577-85. González-Badillo et al., Eur J Sport Sci 2014 (max intended velocity).
Emphasising the stretched position (deep ROM, lengthened partials, e.g., seated leg curl, overhead triceps).
Hypertrophy, especially in the lengthened region; flexibility.
Greater passive + active tension at long lengths appears to amplify the growth signal.
Use full ROM by default; add lengthened partials at end of sets.
Prefer stretched-position variants when choosing between similar combos.
Cutting range short to lift heavier.
Maeo et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2021;53(4):825-37. Pedrosa et al., Eur J Sport Sci 2022. Wolf et al., Int J Strength Cond 2023 (partial vs full ROM meta-analysis).
Maximal strength, neural drive, rate of force development, bone density.
Improves motor-unit recruitment and firing rate, intermuscular coordination, and tendon stiffness.
Main lifts in strength phases; keep ≥1 heavy exposure/week to retain strength.
Grinding to failure on heavy lifts; too little rest.
Schoenfeld et al., J Strength Cond Res 2017;31(12):3508-23. ACSM 2009.
Hypertrophy + strength balance; most time-efficient for size.
High mechanical tension for enough reps, manageable fatigue.
Default for accessory and hypertrophy-phase work.
Treating it as the ONLY range that builds muscle.
Schoenfeld et al., J Strength Cond Res 2017. Schoenfeld 2010 (below).
Light loads ~30–60% 1RM taken close to failure.
Local muscular endurance, capillarisation, hypertrophy (if near failure), joint-friendly.
When sets reach near failure, all motor units are eventually recruited, so growth is similar to heavy loads; strength gains are smaller.
Use for joint-sensitive days, isolation work, rehab and endurance sports.
Stopping light sets far from failure (little stimulus).
Morton et al., J Appl Physiol 2016;121(1):129-38. Schoenfeld et al., J Strength Cond Res 2017.
Quality of subsequent sets → total effective volume.
Longer rest restores phosphocreatine (~90% in 3 min) and lets you keep reps/load high.
Compounds: 2–5 min. Isolation: 1–2 min. Short rest (<60 s) only for density/conditioning goals.
Put rest time in each combo; use supersets (C1) instead of cutting rest when short of time.
Resting 45 s on heavy squats 'for the pump' → less total stimulus.
Schoenfeld et al., J Strength Cond Res 2016;30(7):1805-12. Grgic et al., Eur J Sport Sci 2017;17(8):983-93.
Hypertrophy = increase in muscle fibre cross-sectional area driven by repeated net-positive muscle protein balance.
Muscle size, and indirectly strength potential.
Primary driver: mechanical tension on fibres (sensed via mTORC1 signalling). Metabolic stress plays a supporting role. Muscle damage is NOT required — early 'growth' is often swelling.
≈10–20 hard sets/muscle/week, 6–30 reps within 0–3 RIR, ≥2×/week, full ROM, progressive overload.

sheets.name: Atlas_Explorer

sheets.name: Atlas_Subjects
sheets.title: HUMAN KNOWLEDGE ATLAS — SUBJECTS (MBBS → specialties → physiotherapy → foundations), profiled A→AZ
sheets.subtitle: One row per subject. Read across: what it is → basics → laws → must-remember → advanced → deepest → clinical / physio / sport → upstream & downstream subjects → every cross-link. Codes match Atlas_Topics IDs (e.g. PHY04). Add new subjects in any blank row: AX/AY count topics and links automatically.

sheets.name: Atlas_Topics
sheets.title: HUMAN KNOWLEDGE ATLAS — TOPICS (basic → core → advanced → deep), every topic linked to others by ID
sheets.subtitle: Levels: 1 Basic (must know) · 2 Core (clinical use) · 3 Advanced (specialist) · 4 Deep (integrative / frontier). Column N lists linked topic IDs separated by |; column O explains why they connect; S counts how many topics link back here. Add your own topics in any blank row below (use a new ID like PHY11) — Atlas_Explorer picks them up automatically.

sheets.name: Atlas_Sports
sheets.title: ATLAS SPORTS MAP — every sport linked to its injuries, surgeries, rehab/prevention and performance topics in Atlas_Topics
sheets.subtitle: Columns F–I hold topic IDs (split by |). Column M lists the linked topic names automatically; N flags unknown IDs. Add a sport in any blank row. Atlas_Explorer → Sport lens shows the full topic list for any sport.

sheets.name: Phase_Gates
sheets.title: PHASE GATES — Test Results → Automatic Phase (manual override in Athlete_Profile)
sheets.subtitle: Enter raw test numbers (auto %) or type a final value in MANUAL. Each phase opens when all its thresholds are met and every earlier phase is passed. Thresholds (blue) are editable.

sheets.name: Accelerator_Tree
sheets.title: ACCELERATOR TREE — fast-track, game-based, implicit, loaded and recovery add-ups that feed Full_Pathway columns R→AD
sheets.subtitle: Edit any cell here and every day in Full_Pathway updates. Add your own rows inside the blank slots of each table (games: keep 5 options split by |). Selection rotates by day, phase band (1-6), region group and Heavy/Medium/Light day, so every day gets a new combination. Speed comes from criteria-based progression, never from skipping biological healing floors.

sheets.name: Combo_Generator
sheets.title: COMBO GENERATOR — Live Sandbox: Roll New Combinations of Open/Closed Chain, Short→Long Lever, Gravity, Intent, Mindset and Equipment

sheets.name: Generated_Library
sheets.title: MSX assessment Nov. 2026
sheets.subtitle: 2,192 combinations in batch 1. The loop appends new batches below (rows reserved to 10,004). Mark TRIAL RESULT and rating after you try one — the loop uses your ratings to steer the next batches.

sheets.name: Combo_Dimensions
sheets.title: COMBINATION DIMENSIONS — Building Blocks + Coherence Rules (add your own equipment, mindsets, surfaces, movements)
sheets.subtitle: Lists use |a|b|c| format. For a new movement, fill its allowed stances/equipment/gravity/chains/planes/intents; for a new intent, fill allowed minds (J), modifiers (K), equipment (L, * = any) and gravity (M, * = any). New rows join Combo_Generator instantly and the loop's next batch.

sheets.name: Program_Library
sheets.title: PROGRAM LIBRARY: core programs from warm-up to game-specific, each with its evidence source and level
sheets.subtitle: Each core program is expanded automatically in Program_Variants across every equipment with a matching drill (Equipment_Drills) × level (L1-L4) × 12-week block (B1-B3). Evidence level: A = systematic review/meta-analysis or guideline; B = RCT/controlled study; C = textbook/expert consensus; T = new/unique method, trial it first (Program_Trials).

sheets.name: Program_Trials
sheets.title: PROGRAM TRIALS: try a program, review it, then validate or drop it
sheets.subtitle: How it works: 1) pick a Variant ID from Program_Variants (or a Program ID from Program_Library); 2) test a key measure before (e.g. 10-m sprint, single-leg calf raises, pain on a set task); 3) run the 4-week block and log sessions, RPE and worst pain; 4) re-test; 5) set Verdict to Establish, Modify or Drop. The verdict shows automatically next to that program in Program_Variants and Program_Library. Rule of thumb: Establish only if the key test improved, pain stayed ≤3/10 settling within 24 h, and ≥80% of sessions were completed.

sheets.name: Equipment_Drills
sheets.title: EQUIPMENT DRILLS: equipment-specific drills with instructions, by movement pattern and 12-week block
sheets.subtitle: Key = Equipment|Pattern. Block 1 is the entry drill (weeks 1-4), Block 2 the progression (weeks 5-8), Block 3 the advanced version (weeks 9-12). Program_Variants pulls drills from here; if an equipment has no row for a pattern it falls back to the Bodyweight row. Add your own rows and every program updates.

sheets.name: Program_Dose
sheets.title: PROGRAM DOSE: sets, reps, intensity and rest by quality × level, plus the block (4-week) emphasis
sheets.subtitle: Key = Quality|L1..L4 or Quality|B1..B3. Program_Variants combines one level row and one block row into the dose for each program. Main sources: ACSM 2009 progression position stand; NSCA Essentials (Haff & Triplett 2016); Schoenfeld 2017; Bompa & Buzzichelli 2019.

sheets.name: Program_Variants
sheets.title: PROGRAM VARIANTS (auto-generated): every core program × matching equipment × level × 12-week block
sheets.subtitle: Built by formulas from Program_Library, Equipment_Drills and Program_Dose; do not type in this tab. Add a core program or an equipment drill row and new variants appear here automatically. Each row is a distinct 4-week program block with equipment-specific drills, dose and instructions. Variant ID = Program-Equipment-Level+Block. Status: Established = original program and equipment; 'Adapted equipment' = same program on different equipment (log a trial before relying on it); Trial = our new method.

sheets.name: Sport_Family
sheets.title: SPORT FAMILY: groups each sport by movement profile; drives warm-ups, schedules and games
sheets.subtitle: Left table: sport → family (sport names match Sports_Demands). Right table: family → sports, schedule type and the highest-intensity action the clearance drill must match.

sheets.name: Warmup_Segments
sheets.title: WARM-UP SEGMENTS: the 10-minute warm-up, segment by segment, for each sport family
sheets.subtitle: S1 Mobility 0:00-2:00 → S2 Activation & strength 2:00-3:30 → S3 Loading hold (isometric) 3:30-4:30 → S4 Dynamic movement 4:30-6:30 → S5 Pre-game movement drills 6:30-8:30 → S6 High-intensity clearance 8:30-10:00. Built on RAMP (Jeffreys 2007) and FIFA 11+ (Soligard 2008). Rows below 'STAGE DOSE' set how hard each segment is in each rehab/performance stage (Phase_System).

sheets.name: Warmup_10min
sheets.title: 10-MINUTE WARM-UPS (auto): every sport × stage (22 phases) × day type, mobility to high-intensity clearance
sheets.subtitle: Formulas build each warm-up from Sport_Family, Warmup_Segments and Phase_System; do not type here. S6 'clearance' = 3 reps of the sport's highest-intensity action at or above game intensity before entering the court/field. Fail any rep → no full training that day. Screening flags guide decisions but cannot reliably predict injury (Bahr 2016 BJSM).

sheets.name: Clearance_Drills
sheets.title: CLEARANCE DRILLS: readiness and return-to-play tests that go at or above game demand before full court/field
sheets.subtitle: Use with Phase_Gates. 'Clearance' means the athlete tolerates more than the sport asks of them (3 clean reps at or above game intensity, no flare next day). Honest limit: no screening test reliably predicts who will get injured (Bahr 2016 BJSM); use these to make return and progression decisions and to spot a drop from the athlete's own baseline. Return-to-sport decisions follow the continuum: return to participation → sport → performance (Ardern 2016 BJSM consensus).

sheets.name: Load_Templates
sheets.title: LOAD TEMPLATES: weekly loading pattern by schedule type, with the reasoning, plus stage multipliers
sheets.subtitle: Load = session RPE (1-10) × minutes (arbitrary units, AU) (Foster 2001). Match week assumes a Saturday game (MD = match day). Stage multipliers scale the base load for rehab/performance stage. Keep weekly change within ~10-15% and the acute:chronic ratio ~0.8-1.3 (Gabbett 2016).

sheets.name: Load_Schedule
sheets.title: WEEKLY LOAD SCHEDULE (auto): every sport × stage (1 Protect → 6 Perform) × day, with target load and reasoning
sheets.subtitle: Built from Sport_Family and Load_Templates. Target load is session RPE × minutes (AU), so rate each session after training and compare. The warm-up ID points to the matching 10-minute warm-up in Warmup_10min.

sheets.name: Training_Games
sheets.title: TRAINING GAMES & FUN DRILLS: gamified drills with rules and scoring, for every sport family
sheets.subtitle: Families column lists where each game fits (|ALL| = every family). Drill_Bank expands every game × fitting family × constraint × level. Small-sided and game-based training develop fitness and skill together (Hill-Haas 2011 Sports Med); most fun drills here are coaching practice (level C) or our own designs (T) — log trials in Program_Trials.

sheets.name: Drill_Constraints
sheets.title: DRILL CONSTRAINTS: variations applied to every training game to create the Drill_Bank
sheets.subtitle: Constraints change the problem the athlete solves (constraints-led approach). 'Applies to types' lists the game types each constraint fits.

sheets.name: Drill_Bank
sheets.title: DRILL BANK (auto): every training game × fitting sport family × constraint × level
sheets.subtitle: Built from Training_Games, Sport_Family and Drill_Constraints; do not type here. Add a game or constraint and new drills appear. Drill ID = Game-Family-Constraint-Level, so no drill is listed twice.

sheets.name: Supplements
sheets.title: SUPPLEMENTS — Essential, Sports Foods, Performance, Recovery, Sleep, Adaptogens, Low-Value & High-Risk
sheets.subtitle: Mark USE? = Yes. Doses auto-scale to body mass; warnings come from Athlete_Profile flags; timing feeds Daily_Schedule. Evidence: AIS framework (A strong, B emerging, C weak, D prohibited/high risk). 118 supplements, forms and isomers (rows 16-133); scored atlas in columns AM-BA; below the table: scoring method (row 137), 47 scored brands (row 147), certification schemes (row 197), stacks by level × sport × sex (row 209), dark side of the industry (row 242), protection checklist and sources. Not medical advice — check with a doctor/dietitian, especially with medicines or health conditions.

sheets.name: Condition_Progression
sheets.title: CONDITION PROGRESSION — Every Condition × Phases 1 → 6D × Combined Components, with 3 Same-Goal Alternates and Justification
sheets.subtitle: 52 conditions · 8,736 rows. Filter by Condition and Phase. Alt A = easier but same goal; Alt B = different equipment, same demand; Alt C = different position/plane (for the condition-key exercise: the next progression). Use Day_Planner for the day-by-day version.

sheets.name: Sports_Demands
sheets.title: SPORTS & DEMANDS — Energy Systems, Movements, Qualities, Injuries, KPIs, Unique Skills and Ultimate-Performer Focus
sheets.subtitle: Pick a sport in Day_Planner to pull its 6-level drill ladder into every session.

sheets.name: Sport_Drills
sheets.title: SPORT DRILL LADDERS — 6 Levels per Sport from Skill Retention to Ultimate Performance, each with 3 Alternates
sheets.subtitle: Levels map to phases: L1 = 1C-2C, L2 = 3A-3C, L3 = 4A-4C, L4 = 5A-5C, L5 = 5D-6A, L6 = 6B-6D.

sheets.name: Elite_Methods
sheets.title: ELITE & ULTIMATE-PERFORMANCE METHODS — For Phases 6B/6D and Enhanced-Level Athletes (all legal)
sheets.subtitle: Advanced strength-power, speed, conditioning, environmental, cognitive and programming methods with protocols, readiness criteria and risks.

sheets.name: Phase_System
sheets.title: PHASE SYSTEM — 1 → 1A-1C → 2A-2C → 3A-3C → 4A-4C → 5A-5E → 6A-6D
sheets.subtitle: Every parameter here drives the Session_Builder automatically (goals, depth range, %1RM, sets, reps, tempo, rest). Edit a cell here and every session updates.

sheets.name: Phase_Dose
sheets.title: PHASE DOSE — Numeric Start → End Values that Drive Day-by-Day Progression
sheets.subtitle: Within each phase the Day_Planner moves every dose from 'start' to 'end' as the days pass (then applies heavy/medium/light undulation and readiness). Edit blue cells to change progression.

sheets.name: Conditions_Meta
sheets.title: CONDITIONS — Region, Tissue, Healing Factor and Total Pathway Length
sheets.subtitle: Healing factor scales every phase's base duration (Phase_Dose). Edit the factor (blue) to individualise a condition's timeline.

sheets.name: Testing_Protocols
sheets.title: TESTING PROTOCOLS — How Every Gate Metric Is Measured
sheets.subtitle: Each protocol feeds a metric in Phase_Gates. 'Auto' = enter raw numbers and the % is calculated; 'Manual' = type the final value.

sheets.name: Prohibited_Substances
sheets.title: ANTI-DOPING & 'ENHANCED' SUBSTANCES — WADA Prohibited Classes, Health Risks and Legal Alternatives
sheets.subtitle: Awareness only — no dosing is given. Strict liability: an athlete is responsible for anything found in their sample, including from contaminated supplements. Check medicines on Global DRO and NADA India; use batch-tested products.

sheets.name: Variant_Generator
sheets.title: VARIANT GENERATOR — Build New Exercises from Any Base × Equipment × Loading Strategy × Stance
sheets.subtitle: Pick a base exercise and change equipment/strategy: parameters, depth and reasoning fill in automatically. Copy the green output row and Paste Values into My_Exercises to add it to the session builder.

sheets.name: Loading_Strategies
sheets.title: LOADING STRATEGIES — Parameters Mined from the Library (feeds Variant_Generator)
sheets.subtitle: Each strategy's typical tempo, sets, RPE and rest = the most common value across the library. Depth modifier shows how much harder it makes an exercise.

sheets.name: Depth_Model
sheets.title: DEPTH MODEL — Superficial (L1) to Deepest (L6): How Every Exercise Was Graded
sheets.subtitle: Depth = category baseline adjusted by loading strategy (iso -1; density/cluster/BFR +1; contrast/PAP/explosive +1), RPE (<=4 -1, >=9 +1) and return-to-sport naming. Each exercise has its own reasoning sentence in Exercise_Library.

sheets.name: Exercise_Library
sheets.title: Source Library
sheets.subtitle: Mega Library

sheets.name: Anatomy_Map
sheets.title: ANATOMY MAP: what each base movement loads, activates and trains
sheets.subtitle: One row per base movement. The loop engine reads this tab and adds stance, plane, lever, gravity, intent, equipment and modifier effects to build the anatomy columns (AJ to AR) in Generated_Library. You can edit any cell; new loop runs use your edits. Muscle names match the Anatomy_Reference tab.

sheets.name: Lists
sheets.title: Goals
sheets.subtitle: Mobility

sheets.name: Anatomy_Reference
sheets.title: ANATOMY REFERENCE: every skeletal muscle in the body
sheets.subtitle: 257 named muscles, one per row (muscles with separate heads or parts are split where they work differently). Column H counts left and right plus segmental slips (intercostals, rotatores, interspinales, intertransversarii, levatores costarum): 693 muscles in total. 184 of the 257 (528 of the 693) are loaded by at least one base movement (column I, built from Anatomy_Map). The rest are face, eye, ear, tongue, throat and voice muscles plus a few small ones the current bases don't target.

sheets.name: Training_Science
sheets.title: TRAINING SCIENCE — evidence-based reference for every training variable in this system
sheets.subtitle: How to read: each row is one concept → what it is, what it trains, why it works, the dose research supports, and how to use it here. Evidence level: HIGH = meta-analyses / consensus statements; MODERATE = several controlled trials; EMERGING = limited or mixed data. This is general education, not medical advice — adjust for any condition in Conditions_Meta.
